query: FeCoNi is an fcc alloy with high saturation magnetization and a low coercive field. Earlier studies examined the high-entropy alloys FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt, but both exhibited soft ferromagnetism. A qualifying high-entropy alloy must have an almost equiatomic multicomponent composition and configurational entropy of at least 1.0R. Subject to these constraints, what single intervention could produce a FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloy with greater coercivity than the prior derivatives? Present one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the outcome relative to an appropriate FeCoNi-based baseline, defines the conditions over which it should apply, cites supporting observations from earlier work, and proposes a discriminating experiment with an explicit falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing 20 at.% Al into an equiatomic FeCoNiPd high‐entropy alloy (to form FeCoNiPdAl) will induce the formation of coherent, nanoscale B2‐type Al–Pd‐rich precipitates that pin domain walls and thereby increase the room‐temperature coercive field relative to the FeCoNiPd baseline.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic FeCoNiPd single‐phase fcc high‐entropy alloy, prepared by arc melting and homogenized at 1000 °C for 24 h in vacuum.
generation.intervention: Addition of 20 at.% Al (replacing none of the existing species) to produce an equiatomic quinary FeCoNiPdAl alloy.
generation.conditions: Arc melting under Ar, homogenization at 1000 °C for 24 h, then aging at 500 °C for 24 h under vacuum followed by furnace cooling.
generation.structural_mediator: Nanoscale (20–50 nm) coherent B2‐type Al–Pd‐rich precipitates embedded in the fcc matrix.
generation.mechanism: Domain‐wall pinning at the coherent precipitate/matrix interfaces increases the magnetocrystalline anisotropy and impedes reversal, raising Hc.
generation.predicted_outcome: Room‐temperature coercivity Hc increases from ~20 Oe in FeCoNiPd to >100 Oe in FeCoNiPdAl (i.e. ≥5× baseline).
generation.baseline: Equiatomic FeCoNiPd HEA processed under identical thermal treatments, exhibiting Hc ≈20 Oe at 300 K.
generation.boundary: Applies only to equiatomic FeCoNiPdAl compositions prepared and aged under the specified thermal schedule; other compositions, heat treatments, or non‐equiatomic ratios may not form the requisite B2 precipitates.
generation.uncertainty: Moderate; the kinetics and thermodynamics of Al–Pd ordering in this specific quinary are not established and may require optimization of aging parameters.

falsification_experiment.design: Synthesize two specimens: (1) equiatomic FeCoNiPd and (2) equiatomic FeCoNiPdAl. Apply identical arc‐melting, homogenization (1000 °C/24 h), and aging (500 °C/24 h) treatments. Characterize microstructure by TEM and measure magnetic hysteresis at 300 K using VSM.
measurements: TEM imaging and EDS mapping to detect and size Al–Pd precipitates
Magnetic hysteresis loops to extract coercive field Hc
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If TEM shows no coherent B2‐type Al–Pd precipitates in FeCoNiPdAl or if its Hc does not exceed the FeCoNiPd baseline by at least a factor of two, the hypothesis is falsified.
